channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SecureWebArena, a holistic security evaluation benchmark for LVLM-based web agents.
  • Introduces six simulated web environments and 2,970 trajectories covering diverse tasks and attack settings.
  • Defines a taxonomy of six attack vectors spanning user-level and environment-level manipulations.
  • Uses a multi-layer evaluation protocol (internal reasoning, behavioral trajectory, task outcome) and reports vulnerabilities across nine LVLM agent variants.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zonghao Ying', 'Yangguang Shao', 'Jianle Gan', 'Gan Xu', 'Wenxin Zhang', 'Quanchen Zou', 'Junzheng Shi', 'Zhenfei Yin', 'Mingchuan Zhang', 'Aishan Liu', 'Xianglong Liu']
  • Tags: ['AI Security Evaluation', 'Adversarial Attacks', 'Web Agents', 'LVLM', 'Red Teaming/Benchmark']

item.title: EDGE-Shield: Efficient Denoising-staGE Shield for Violative Content Filtering via Scalable Reference-Based Matching
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes EDGE-Shield, a training-free, reference-based content filtering method for text-to-image generative models.
  • Uses embedding-based reference matching and an x-pred latent transformation to classify violative content earlier during the denoising process.
  • Targets risks including copyright violation and deepfake generation by blocking violative outputs during generation.
  • Evaluated on Z-Image-Turbo and Qwen-Image, showing significant latency reductions while maintaining filtering accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Takara Taniguchi', 'Ryohei Shimizu', 'Duc Minh Vo', 'Kota Izumi', 'Shiqi Yang', 'Teppei Suzuki']
  • Tags: ['content filtering', 'violative/deepfake detection', 'reference-based matching', 'generative model defenses', 'text-to-image']

item.title: Causal Fingerprints of AI Generative Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “causal fingerprints” for generative models to improve source attribution beyond artifact/model-specific cues.
  • Introduces a causality-decoupling framework to disentangle fingerprint signals from image content/style using a semantic-invariant latent space.
  • Validates via attribution across representative GANs and diffusion models and demonstrates source anonymization using counterfactual examples.
  • Claims improved performance for applications like forgery detection, copyright tracing, and identity protection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hui Xu', 'Chi Liu', 'Congcong Zhu', 'Minghao Wang', 'Youyang Qu', 'Longxiang Gao']
  • Tags: ['model attribution', 'source fingerprinting', 'generative forensics', 'anonymization/counterfactuals', 'GANs & diffusion']

item.title: Retrievals Can Be Detrimental: Unveiling the Backdoor Vulnerability of Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes BadRDM, a multimodal contrastive attack targeting retrieval-augmented diffusion models (RDMs).
  • Shows how attackers can manipulate retrieved items via text triggers and inserted poisoned “target toxicity surrogates” in the retrieval database.
  • Injects backdoors into the retriever so triggers reliably lead to toxic/undesired generated outputs while keeping benign utility largely intact.
  • Uses entropy-based selection and generative augmentation to improve the effectiveness of the poisoning/backdoor surrogates.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hao Fang', 'Xiaohang Sui', 'Hongyao Yu', 'Kuofeng Gao', 'Jiawei Kong', 'Sijin Yu', 'Bin Chen', 'Shu-Tao Xia']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'retrieval-augmented generation', 'diffusion models', 'multimodal attacks', 'data poisoning']

item.title: Scaling Exposes the Trigger: Input-Level Backdoor Detection in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Cross-Attention Scaling
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies backdoor security risks in text-to-image diffusion models and focuses on input-level backdoor detection.
  • Introduces a probing method using cross-attention scaling perturbations to reveal a detection signal (CSRD) across denoising steps.
  • Proposes SET, a trigger-agnostic detection framework that learns benign response space from clean samples and flags deviations.
  • Evaluates against multiple backdoor attack methods/trigger types and reports improved detection metrics (AUROC/ACC).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zida Li', 'Jun Li', 'Yuzhe Sha', 'Ziqiang Li', 'Lizhi Xiong', 'Zhangjie Fu']
  • Tags: ['Backdoor Detection', 'Text-to-Image Diffusion', 'Cross-Attention Probing', 'Stealthy Triggers', 'Adversarial Security']

item.title: Decoding by Perturbation: Mitigating MLLM Hallucinations via Dynamic Textual Perturbation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Decoding by Perturbation (DeP), a training-free method to mitigate hallucinations in multimodal LLMs by applying dynamic textual perturbations during decoding.
  • Uses attention variance and logit statistics to reduce overreliance on language priors and suppress suspicious visual grounding noise.
  • Targets a security-adjacent failure mode (hallucination) rather than classic adversarial attacks, aiming to make grounding more faithful during inference.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Sihang Jia', 'Shuliang Liu', 'Songbo Yang', 'Yibo Yan', 'Xin Zou', 'Xuming Hu']
  • Tags: ['hallucination-mitigation', 'multimodal-LLM', 'decoding-time-interventions', 'textual-perturbation', 'robustness']

item.title: CoLA: A Choice Leakage Attack Framework to Expose Privacy Risks in Subset Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CoLA (Choice Leakage Attack) to study privacy leakage arising from subset training and data inclusion/exclusion choices.
  • Defines two attack scenarios: subset-aware side-channel attacks using metadata from selection, and black-box attacks using only model outputs.
  • Introduces two privacy leakage targets: training-membership MIA (TM-MIA) and selection-participation MIA (SP-MIA) covering samples involved in the subset selection process.
  • Empirically shows subset training can increase privacy risk beyond standard expectations, leaking both training and selection membership across vision and language models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Qi Li', 'Cheng-Long Wang', 'Yinzhi Cao', 'Di Wang']
  • Tags: ['privacy attacks', 'membership inference', 'data subset selection', 'side-channel leakage', 'black-box privacy attacks']

item.title: Challenging Vision-Language Models with Physically Deployable Multimodal Semantic Lighting Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes MSLA, a physically deployable adversarial lighting attack framework targeting vision-language models (VLMs).
  • Demonstrates that controllable adversarial lighting can disrupt multimodal semantic understanding, causing recognition failures and semantic hallucinations rather than only specific output errors.
  • Shows degradation of zero-shot classification in CLIP variants and severe semantic misinterpretation in LLaVA and BLIP for image captioning and VQA.
  • Provides evidence of cross-domain effectiveness with experiments in both digital and physical settings, including transferability and practical realizability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yingying Zhao', 'Chengyin Hu', 'Qike Zhang', 'Xin Li', 'Xin Wang', 'Yiwei Wei', 'Jiujiang Guo', 'Jiahuan Long', 'Tingsong Jiang', 'Wen Yao']
  • Tags: ['physical adversarial attacks', 'vision-language models (VLMs)', 'multimodal semantic attacks', 'semantic hallucination']

item.title: Generative Anonymization in Event Streams
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a generative anonymization framework for neuromorphic event streams to prevent identity recovery from Event-to-Video (E2V) reconstructions.
  • Projects event data into an intensity representation, uses pretrained generative models to synthesize non-existent identities, then re-encodes back to the neuromorphic domain.
  • Introduces a synchronized real-world event+RGB dataset (via robotic trajectories) as a benchmark for privacy-preserving evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Adam T. M\\"uller', 'Mihai Kocsis', 'Nicolaj C. Stache']
  • Tags: ['privacy-preserving ML', 'anonymization', 'neuromorphic vision', 'identity inference', 'generative models']

item.title: Fragile Reconstruction: Adversarial Vulnerability of Reconstruction-Based Detectors for Diffusion-Generated Images
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that reconstruction-based detectors for diffusion-generated images are highly vulnerable to imperceptible adversarial perturbations, driving detection accuracy near zero.
  • Performs systematic white-box adversarial attacks and demonstrates transferability across different detectors and generative backbones, including black-box viability.
  • Evaluates countermeasures and finds standard adversarial defenses offer limited mitigation, attributing failure to low signal-to-noise ratio for attacked samples.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Haoyang Jiang', 'Mingyang Yi', 'Shaolei Zhang', 'Junxian Cai', 'Qingbin Liu', 'Xi Chen', 'Ju Fan']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-robustness', 'ai-generated-image-detection', 'diffusion-models', 'adversarial-attacks', 'detector-evasion']

item.title: Efficient Adversarial Training via Criticality-Aware Fine-Tuning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Criticality-Aware Adversarial Training (CAAT) to improve robustness of Vision Transformers by fine-tuning only a small, robustness-critical subset of parameters.
  • Uses parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to selectively adapt modules/weight matrices based on estimated criticality for adversarial robustness.
  • Finds that scaling to larger ViT models maintains robustness comparable to standard adversarial training with much lower computational cost and far fewer trainable parameters.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenyun Li', 'Zheng Zhang', 'Dongmei Jiang', 'Yaowei Wang', 'Xiangyuan Lan']
  • Tags: ['adversarial training', 'robustness', 'vision transformers', 'parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)', 'model robustness defenses']

item.title: Reading Between the Pixels: Linking Text-Image Embedding Alignment to Typographic Attack Success on Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies typographic prompt injection attacks on vision-language models by rendering adversarial text as images to bypass safety mechanisms.
  • Evaluates attack success across multiple VLMs using SALAD-Bench prompts under varying font sizes and visual transformations (rotation, blur, noise, contrast).
  • Finds strong relationships between text-image embedding alignment/distance (via multimodal embedding models) and attack success rate.
  • Analyzes how degradations and rotation affect vulnerability differently across models, indicating model-specific robustness patterns.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ravikumar Balakrishnan', 'Sanket Mendapara', 'Ankit Garg']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection', 'typographic attacks', 'vision-language models', 'attack evaluation', 'embedding alignment']

item.title: Boosting Robust AIGI Detection with LoRA-based Pairwise Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a LoRA-based pairwise training method to improve robustness of AI-generated image (AIGI) detectors under in-the-wild distortions.
  • Uses targeted finetuning of a visual foundation model plus simulated distortions/size changes during training to match deployment data distribution.
  • Evaluates on a robust AIGI detection challenge setting and reports competitive results (3rd place).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ruiyang Xia', 'Qi Zhang', 'Yaowen Xu', 'Zhaofan Zou', 'Hao Sun', 'Zhongjiang He', 'Xuelong Li']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'Robustness', 'LoRA fine-tuning', 'Adversarial/in-the-wild distortions', 'Computer vision security']

item.title: Curvelet-Based Frequency-Aware Feature Enhancement for Deepfake Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a Curvelet-transform-based deepfake detector that enhances discriminative frequency features.
  • Uses wedge-level attention and scale-aware spatial masking to emphasize robust cues under compression.
  • Reconstructs refined frequency cues and feeds them into a modified pretrained Xception network for classification.
  • Evaluates on FaceForensics++ across compression qualities, reporting very high accuracy/AUC, especially under low compression.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Salar Adel Sabri', 'Ramadhan J. Mstafa']
  • Tags: ['deepfake detection', 'frequency-domain features', 'Curvelet transform', 'adversarial/forgery robustness', 'computer vision security']

item.title: UniMark: Unified Adaptive Multi-bit Watermarking for Autoregressive Image Generators
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes UniMark, a training-free watermarking framework for autoregressive image generators to enable multi-bit invisible watermark messages.
  • Introduces adaptive semantic codebook partitioning using a secret key to improve security against watermark-related attacks after exposure.
  • Uses block-wise multi-bit encoding with error-correcting codes for reliable extraction and a unified embedding interface across AR image generation paradigms.
  • Evaluates robustness against common transformations (e.g., cropping, JPEG, noise, blur) and reports improved detection/multi-bit extraction along with image quality metrics.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yigit Yilmaz', 'Elena Petrova', 'Mehmet Kaya', 'Lucia Rossi', 'Amir Rahman']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'Invisible/robust watermarking', 'Autoregressive image generation', 'Multi-bit encoding', 'Robustness against transformations']

item.title: GigaCheck: Detecting LLM-generated Content via Object-Centric Span Localization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GigaCheck, a dual-strategy system to detect AI-generated text.
  • Uses a document-level fine-tuned LLM representation for authorship (AI vs human) classification.
  • Introduces span-level “object-centric” localization using a DETR-like architecture adapted to text to localize AI-generated intervals.
  • Evaluated on multiple classification and localization benchmarks and releases code for reproducibility.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Irina Tolstykh', 'Aleksandra Tsybina', 'Sergey Yakubson', 'Aleksandr Gordeev', 'Vladimir Dokholyan', 'Maksim Kuprashevich']
  • Tags: ['LLM-generated text detection', 'Span localization', 'Authorship attribution', 'DETR-like localization', 'Robustness']

item.title: RePAIR: Interactive Machine Unlearning through Prompt-Aware Model Repair
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an interactive machine unlearning paradigm where users can request forgetting via natural-language prompts at inference time.
  • Introduces RePAIR, a prompt-aware repair framework using a watchdog (intent detection), a surgeon model (repair procedure generation), and an autonomously updated patient model.
  • Develops STAMP, a training-free single-sample unlearning method that redirects activations toward a refusal subspace using closed-form pseudoinverse updates, including a low-rank variant for efficiency.
  • Evaluates on harmful knowledge suppression, misinformation correction, and personal data erasure, reporting near-zero forget metrics while largely preserving utility.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jagadeesh Rachapudi', 'Pranav Singh', 'Ritali Vatsi', 'Praful Hambarde', 'Amit Shukla']
  • Tags: ['Machine Unlearning', 'LLM Safety/Alignment', 'Prompt-Aware Model Editing', 'Privacy/Data Erasure']

item.title: LASA: Language-Agnostic Semantic Alignment at the Semantic Bottleneck for LLM Safety
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes LASA (Language-Agnostic Semantic Alignment) to improve LLM safety in low-resource languages by aligning safety behavior at a semantic bottleneck layer.
  • Identifies a representation-space “semantic bottleneck” where shared semantic content dominates over language identity.
  • Reports substantial reductions in reported attack success rate (ASR) when applying LASA across multiple LLM families and languages.
  • Frames safety as a representation-level issue caused by safety alignment bias toward high-resource languages.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Junxiao Yang', 'Haoran Liu', 'Jinzhe Tu', 'Jiale Cheng', 'Zhexin Zhang', 'Shiyao Cui', 'Jiaqi Weng', 'Jialing Tao', 'Hui Xue', 'Hongning Wang', 'Han Qiu', 'Minlie Huang']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'semantic alignment', 'cross-lingual robustness', 'adversarial attack evaluation', 'representation learning']

item.title: Compiling Activation Steering into Weights via Null-Space Constraints for Stealthy Backdoors
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a method to implant stealthy backdoors into LLMs by converting activation steering into persistent weight edits.
  • Uses a null-space constraint to keep the backdoor dormant on clean inputs, preserving benign behavior and stealthiness.
  • Shifts the backdoor objective from surface token mapping to internal representation steering for more reliable sustained malicious output under a hidden trigger.
  • Evaluated on multiple safety-aligned LLMs and jailbreak benchmarks, focusing on high triggered attack success with maintained general utility.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rui Yin', 'Tianxu Han', 'Naen Xu', 'Changjiang Li', 'Ping He', 'Chunyi Zhou', 'Jun Wang', 'Zhihui Fu', 'Tianyu Du', 'Jinbao Li', 'Shouling Ji']
  • Tags: ['backdoored models', 'stealthy attacks', 'jailbreaking', 'weight editing', 'activation steering']

item.title: Policy-Invisible Violations in LLM-Based Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a security/policy failure mode for LLM agents: actions that appear valid and appropriate can still violate organizational policy due to missing hidden facts (entity attributes, contextual state, or session history) at decision time.
  • Introduces the PhantomPolicy benchmark with eight policy-violation categories and corresponding safe-control cases, using tool responses that omit policy metadata.
  • Proposes Sentinel, an enforcement framework that simulates the post-action world state via counterfactual graph execution and checks invariants to decide Allow/Block/Clarify.
  • Shows Sentinel improves over a content-only DLP baseline on human-reviewed trace labels, highlighting benefits of world-state-grounded enforcement.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jie Wu', 'Ming Gong']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'policy enforcement', 'security benchmarking', 'guardrails', 'world-state simulation']

item.title: CompliBench: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Compliance Violation Detection in Dialogue Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CompliBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM-judge reliability in detecting and localizing compliance/guideline violations in multi-turn dialogue systems.
  • Introduces an automated, controllable flaw-injection pipeline with adversarial search to generate realistic and challenging policy-violation dialogues with ground-truth labels.
  • Finds that current SOTA proprietary LLM judges perform poorly on compliance violation detection.
  • Shows that fine-tuning a small judge model on the synthesized benchmark improves performance and generalizes across domains, supporting training of reward models.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jingbo Yang', 'Guanyu Yao', 'Bairu Hou', 'Xinghan Yang', 'Nikolai Glushnev', 'Iwona Bialynicka-Birula', 'Duo Ding', 'Shiyu Chang']
  • Tags: ['LLM-as-a-judge', 'Compliance violation detection', 'Adversarial data generation', 'Dialogue safety evaluation', 'Benchmarking']

item.title: Malice in Agentland: Down the Rabbit Hole of Backdoors in the AI Supply Chain
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows how adversaries can poison multiple stages of the AI agent supply chain to implant stealthy backdoors.
  • Defines and evaluates three threat models: poisoning finetuning data, using pre-backdoored base models, and a novel 'environment poisoning' attack against agentic training pipelines.
  • Demonstrates backdoor triggers can lead to unsafe/malicious behavior, including confidential data leakage with >80% success on agent benchmarks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ["L\\'eo Boisvert", 'Abhay Puri', 'Chandra Kiran Reddy Evuru', 'Nazanin Sepahvand', 'Nicolas Chapados', 'Quentin Cappart', 'Alexandre Lacoste', 'Krishnamurthy Dj Dvijotham', 'Alexandre Drouin']
  • Tags: ['Backdoor attacks', 'Data poisoning', 'Agentic AI supply chain security', 'Threat modeling']

item.title: Poisoning the Inner Prediction Logic of Graph Neural Networks for Clean-Label Backdoor Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes BA-Logic, a clean-label backdoor attack method for Graph Neural Networks where training labels cannot be modified.
  • Identifies prior clean-label graph backdoor methods as failing because they cannot sufficiently poison the model’s internal prediction logic so triggers are treated as unimportant.
  • Uses a coordinated poisoned node selector and logic-poisoning trigger generator to improve backdoor attack success rate.
  • Reports experimental results on real-world graph datasets showing improved performance over existing clean-label graph backdoor attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuxiang Zhang', 'Bin Ma', 'Enyan Dai']
  • Tags: ['clean-label backdoor attacks', 'graph neural networks', 'data poisoning', 'adversarial attacks', 'backdoor trigger generation']

item.title: Hail to the Thief: Exploring Attacks and Defenses in Decentralised GRPO
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and studies adversarial attacks against decentralized GRPO via malicious nodes that share poisoned completions to poison benign participants.
  • Shows high effectiveness of the attacks (up to 100% success rate in as few as 50 iterations) on math and coding tasks.
  • Introduces two defenses: (1) filtering using checks on logit probabilities of completions and (2) using an LLM judge to filter completions.
  • Finds defenses eliminate most attack types, except a denial-of-service attack that yields overly long but still conceptually correct completions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Nikolay Blagoev', 'O\\u{g}uzhan Ersoy', 'Lydia Yiyu Chen']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'data poisoning', 'reinforcement learning for LLMs', 'decentralized training', 'defense/filtering']

item.title: GTCN-G: A Residual Graph-Temporal Fusion Network for Imbalanced Intrusion Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GTCN-G, a deep model combining gated temporal convolution (G-TCN) with graph convolution (GCN) for intrusion detection.
  • Uses residual learning via a graph attention network (GAT) to preserve features and improve detection of minority malicious classes under class imbalance.
  • Evaluates on UNSW-NB15 and ToN-IoT, reporting state-of-the-art results for binary and multi-class intrusion detection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tianxiang Xu', 'Zhichao Wen', 'Xinyu Zhao', 'Qi Hu', 'Yan Li', 'Chang Liu']
  • Tags: ['intrusion detection', 'network security', 'class-imbalance', 'graph neural networks', 'time-series modeling']

item.title: Towards Generalized Certified Robustness with Multi-Norm Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CURE, a multi-norm certified training framework to improve “union robustness” across multiple perturbation types/norms (e.g., l∞, l2) and additional transformations (geometric, patch).
  • Develops a theoretical framework to analyze tradeoffs between certifiable robustness under different perturbation sets.
  • Implements bound-alignment strategies and shows improved certified robustness and better performance on unseen geometric/patch perturbations compared to state-of-the-art certified training.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Enyi Jiang', 'David S. Cheung', 'Gagandeep Singh']
  • Tags: ['certified robustness', 'adversarial robustness', 'multi-norm training', 'robustness certification']

item.title: Generative Anonymization in Event Streams
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a generative anonymization framework for neuromorphic event streams to prevent identity recovery from event-to-video reconstructions.
  • Uses an intermediate intensity representation with pretrained generative models to synthesize non-existent identities, then re-encodes back into the neuromorphic event domain.
  • Introduces a synchronized real-world event+RGB dataset/benchmark for evaluating privacy-preserving transformations in neuromorphic vision.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Adam T. M\\"uller', 'Mihai Kocsis', 'Nicolaj C. Stache']
  • Tags: ['privacy-preserving ML', 'anonymization', 'event-to-video reconstruction', 'neuromorphic vision', 'membership/identity leakage evaluation']

item.title: Evaluating Differential Privacy Against Membership Inference in Federated Learning: Insights from the NIST Genomics Red Team Challenge
item.description:
Summary

  • Evaluates Differential Privacy (DP) as a defense against membership inference attacks (MIAs) in Federated Learning (FL).
  • Proposes a stacking-based attack that ensembles black-box estimators and trains a meta-classifier using prediction probabilities and losses.
  • Measures membership leakage across different DP privacy budgets (ε=∞, ε=200, ε=10) using the NIST Genomics PPFL red teaming environment.
  • Finds that while higher DP reduces leakage, measurable leakage persists at ε=200 and stacking attacks remain effective.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Gustavo de Carvalho Bertoli']
  • Tags: ['membership inference', 'differential privacy', 'federated learning', 'privacy attacks', 'red teaming']

item.title: ProbeLogits: Kernel-Level LLM Inference Primitives for AI-Native Operating Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ProbeLogits, a kernel-level LLM inference primitive that performs a forward pass and reads specific token logits to classify agent actions as safe vs dangerous.
  • Implements OS-level governance below the WASM sandbox boundary to make policy enforcement harder to bypass than application-layer classifiers.
  • Evaluates on an OS action benchmark with adversarial-attack categories and on ToxicChat, reporting strong F1 performance and tunable calibration strength (α) for policy tradeoffs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Daeyeon Son']
  • Tags: ['AI safety governance', 'LLM moderation/classification', 'Kernel-level security', 'Adversarial robustness evaluation']

item.title: Understanding and Improving Continuous Adversarial Training for LLMs via In-context Learning Theory
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes continuous adversarial training (CAT) for LLMs through the lens of in-context learning theory.
  • Provides theoretical results (robust generalization bounds) linking embedding-space perturbations to improved robustness against jailbreak attacks.
  • Proposes an additional embedding-matrix singular-value regularization to improve the jailbreak robustness–utility tradeoff.
  • Validates the approach with experiments on real-world LLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shaopeng Fu', 'Di Wang']
  • Tags: ['adversarial training', 'jailbreak defense', 'robustness bounds', 'LLM theory', 'in-context learning']

item.title: GF-Score: Certified Class-Conditional Robustness Evaluation with Fairness Guarantees
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GF-Score, a certified class-conditional robustness evaluation framework that reports per-class robustness profiles rather than a single aggregate score.
  • Introduces fairness/disparity metrics (RDI, NRGC, WCR, FP-GREAT) to quantify how robustness varies across classes.
  • Presents a self-calibration procedure to reduce dependence on adversarial attacks, using clean accuracy correlations to tune a temperature parameter.
  • Evaluates 22 models on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet using RobustBench-certified robustness metrics and analyzes class-wise vulnerability patterns.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Arya Shah', 'Kaveri Visavadiya', 'Manisha Padala']
  • Tags: ['certified robustness', 'fairness evaluation', 'adversarial robustness', 'robustness auditing', 'certification']

item.description:

Summary

  • Addresses safety alignment degradation during LLM fine-tuning (“safety drift”).
  • Proposes Coupled Weight and Activation Constraints (CWAC) that jointly constrain weight updates and activation behavior tied to safety-critical features.
  • Reports experiments showing reduced harmful outputs with minimal loss in fine-tuning accuracy, including under high proportions of harmful data.

item.title: Policy-Invisible Violations in LLM-Based Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a security/policy failure mode for LLM agents: actions that appear valid and appropriate can still violate organizational policy due to missing hidden facts (entity attributes, contextual state, or session history) at decision time.
  • Introduces the PhantomPolicy benchmark with eight policy-violation categories and corresponding safe-control cases, using tool responses that omit policy metadata.
  • Proposes Sentinel, an enforcement framework that simulates the post-action world state via counterfactual graph execution and checks invariants to decide Allow/Block/Clarify.
  • Shows Sentinel improves over a content-only DLP baseline on human-reviewed trace labels, highlighting benefits of world-state-grounded enforcement.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'policy enforcement', 'security benchmarking', 'guardrails', 'world-state simulation']
